wc_specific_findings.states_part_three_other_states: All states and U.S. territories EXCEPT ND, OH, WA, WY, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, and Arizona
wc_specific_findings.monopolistic_state_exposure: Other States coverage explicitly excludes the four monopolistic states (ND, OH, WA, WY). If Precision Aero has any employees traveling to or working in these states, separate state-fund coverage is required — there is NO carrier-provided coverage for monopolistic states.
wc_specific_findings.waiver_of_subrogation_note: No Waiver of Subrogation endorsement (WC 00 03 13) appears in the schedule of endorsements on the Information Page. For an aerospace/manufacturing operation supplying OEMs (Boeing, Lockheed, defense primes), Tier-1 supplier contracts almost universally require Waiver of Subrogation in favor of the customer. Absent endorsement = the carrier retains full subrogation rights against any party who caused an employee injury, including the very customers Precision Aero is contractually obligated to protect. Recommend adding a blanket Waiver of Subrogation endorsement.
wc_specific_findings.alternate_employer_note: No Alternate Employer endorsement (WC 00 03 01 A) is listed. Given the Named Insured includes Black Mountain Investment Company LLC (likely a holding/real-estate affiliate), confirm whether any employees are payrolled through one entity but performing work for the other. If so, an Alternate Employer endorsement is appropriate.
wc_specific_findings.voluntary_compensation_note: No Voluntary Compensation endorsement noted. For Precision Aero specifically this is likely non-issue (manufacturing employees should be statutory employees in AZ), but verify if any executives/owners are excluded from statutory coverage and would benefit from voluntary coverage.
wc_specific_findings.uslh_maritime_note: USL&H / Maritime coverage not endorsed. Aerospace manufacturing in landlocked Arizona — likely non-applicable. Verify whether any operations involve seaplane/amphibious aircraft work near navigable waters, otherwise no concern.
wc_specific_findings.experience_mod_note: EMR factor not visible in the extracted Information Page text. WC 00 04 25 endorsement permits mid-term EMR revision per NCCI. Obtain current EMR and 3-year trend for full audit.
wc_specific_findings.classification_codes_note: Dec page references 'REFER TO NEXT PAGE FOR COMPLETE INFORMATION' for class codes, payroll, and rates — those classification pages were not contained in the extracted excerpt. Cannot evaluate class code accuracy for aerospace manufacturing operations from text provided. Pull complete dec/classification schedule from carrier to verify code(s) match Precision Aero's actual operations (likely 3681 Instrument Mfg. NOC, 3076 Fireproof Equipment Mfg., or aerospace-specific code depending on work performed).
wc_specific_findings.audit_noncompliance_penalty_severity: Audit Noncompliance Charge endorsement (WC 00 04 24) permits Pekin to charge up to 2x estimated annual premium for failure to cooperate with audit. With $18,533 estimated annual premium, worst-case penalty is ~$37,066. Not unusual but material — ensure premium audit responsiveness.

structural_observations.named_insured_status: Primary Named Insured (Precision Aero Inc) is a Corporation. Affiliate Black Mountain Investment Company LLC is properly added to the Named Insured field via a Name Overflow endorsement (WC 97 06 01) — this is a direct amendment, not a conditional Broad Form extension, so the LLC IS reliably covered as an insured employer under this policy. No GAP-01 LLC-exclusion risk on this WC policy.
structural_observations.other_states_coverage_quality: Part Three (Other States) is broadly written — all U.S. states and territories except the four monopolistic states, Puerto Rico, USVI, and AZ (which is on Part One). For a single-location AZ operation with potential field/installation travel, this is appropriate scope.
structural_observations.premium_size: $18,533 estimated annual premium is small for a manufacturing operation — verify payroll basis and class codes are accurate; under-reported payroll will produce a sizeable audit premium.
